title: Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute's muscle-signal “smart hand” lets bilateral amputee Wang Bing eat, drink, shake hands and write his name
summary: Guangming Daily (13 August 2024): Wang Bing, who lost both hands, uses the institute's algorithm-decoded “smart hand” to eat with a spoon, drink, shake hands, rotate his wrist and write his name.
account: A Guangming Daily feature (13 August 2024) on Chongqing's Liangjiang New Area opens with Wang Bing. He lost both hands in an accident a few years earlier, leaving half of each forearm. He says he now uses the “smart hand” to eat with a spoon, drink from a cup, shake hands and rotate his wrist. He manages daily life alone and can grip a pen and write his name. Xie Haiqiong, director of the Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute at Mingyue Lake, says researchers devised a scheme. It detects and identifies electrical signals at suitable muscle sites and processes them by algorithmic analysis. So the user controls the hand by intention, not passive motion. Fiscal funds arriving since 2023 under the district's grant-to-equity model supported the project. The institute formed a company to incubate the exoskeleton project (Guangming Daily via Haiwainet and NetEase). The fitting date is not given.
purpose: Built to let a person with amputated hands control a prosthetic hand through muscle signals. The daily-task function Wang Bing describes is that purpose. The feature frames the project as an example of the district's policy for commercializing research.
system: 'Smart hand' (智能手) muscle-signal prosthetic hand from the institute's exoskeleton robot project
developer: Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute (重庆生物智能制造研究院), Liangjiang New Area

ratings.reason: Per Guangming Daily, Wang Bing, who lost both hands, says he eats with a spoon, drinks from a cup, shakes hands and rotates his wrist. He writes his name and manages daily life alone with the device. A capability restored, reported in his words without clinical assessment.

ai_role.statement: The only description of the technology is institute director Xie Haiqiong's, as quoted by Guangming Daily. It is a scheme that detects and identifies electrical signals at suitable muscle sites and processes them by algorithmic analysis. That lets the user control the hand by intention. No source names a machine-learning method, model, training procedure or accuracy figure. The Monitor's “AI-driven” label rests on that description. The functional gains are Wang Bing's own account in a newspaper feature about the district's commercialization policy. No clinician or independent evaluation is cited.

fields.account: A Guangming Daily feature (13 August 2024) on Chongqing's Liangjiang New Area opens with Wang Bing. He lost both hands in an accident a few years earlier, leaving half of each forearm. He says he now uses the “smart hand” to eat with a spoon, drink from a cup, shake hands and rotate his wrist. He manages daily life alone and can grip a pen and write his name. Xie Haiqiong, director of the Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute at Mingyue Lake, says researchers devised a scheme. It detects and identifies electrical signals at suitable muscle sites and processes them by algorithmic analysis. So the user controls the hand by intention, not passive motion. Fiscal funds arriving since 2023 under the district's grant-to-equity model supported the project. The institute formed a company to incubate the exoskeleton project (Guangming Daily via Haiwainet and NetEase). The fitting date is not given.
